item.title: China Open Source Daily — 2026-11-13
item.description: On 2026-11-13 two instruments converted a person into something portable. OpenAtom opened registration for its open-source talent certification exam -- five tracks at the 2026 Developer Conference in Zhengzhou on 20-21 November, open-source general knowledge plus OpenHarmony engineer and senior engineer, openEuler engineer and openKylin engineer -- and stated plainly that the exam charges a fee, that all revenue is ring-fenced for building the certification system and open-source education, and that the credential makes capability 'measurable, recognisable and circulable.' The foundation's certification page shows four project ladders already standing behind the notice, each with three tiers ending at expert engineer, none of them a maintainer or governance track. The same day Global Times ran a feature pairing a genuine technical contribution with a national frame: ForgeKernel, the Tsinghua and ModelBest self-evolving kernel-generation system, is Apache-2.0 on GitHub (290 stars, 39 forks, 6 open issues, a published v1.5 TODO) with a CC BY 4.0 paper, and as of 2026-10-30 it led all three CANN-Bench 2.0 leaderboards on Ascend and NVIDIA's SOL-ExecBench FlashInfer-Bench track -- the first system to top both a Chinese and an American kernel leaderboard. Wrapped around it was the other instrument: 47 teachers from 34 countries who spent two weeks in Beijing on BAAI's FlagOS stack, part of a programme reporting 350+ applications from 48+ countries and pilot delivery with the African Union's ASRIC, framed by a Renmin University white paper arguing models, compute and corpora should be global digital public goods. One story sells a credential to a domestic developer; the other gives a foreign academic a capability. Both convert a person into a carrier. Neither converts a person into a maintainer -- and that is the week.
